newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - March jobs vigil continues.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - March jobs vigil continues.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds ended flat to slightly higher Thursday heading into Friday's March employment report.
"Nobody is doing anything, and the excuse is employment tomorrow," a municipal analyst said. "That's what everybody is waiting for."
The analyst judged high-grade issues unchanged, and dollar bonds flat to "up a couple of ticks."
A trader differed, however, assessing the overall market up "a solid quarter."

"It just seems like we've finally got some people willing to buy a little bit, and we've had a better tone for the last two or three days," the trader said, adding that a handful of customers might be behind the rise.
"I don't think there's a lot of bonds offered in the market, so it doesn't take very much," he said.

Thursday's bid lists amounted to the "usual array," the trader said, "no more, no less." Earlier in the session traders cited limited selling as it appeared that players had positions set ahead of the jobs news.

Economists polled by Reuters expect March non-farm payrolls to grow by 196,000 versus February's 339,000 rise. The estimate was higher than an earlier consensus forecast, which called for a 182,000 jobs rise.
"You know I don't think people are too afraid of it," the trader said.
While the possibility of an unwelcome surprise always exists, the bond market has been "sold enough" of late and buyers have cash, he said.

"I think they have accumulated enough money so that they are going to spend it," the trader said. "If it goes down a little bit tomorrow, I think they will still spend it, but I don't hear anybody really all that concerned."
The impending report, however, led New York City to delay its $900 million bond sale by one day until April 9 so that it could start taking retail orders after the jobs report's release.
In other news, Standard & Poor's Corp upgraded $8.2 billion of Florida full faith and credit debt to AA-plus from AA.
Shortly after the news, a trader cited little change in Florida bonds.

"We haven't seen anything that would be material," he said. "I just don't think it's going to make a measurable impact in the secondary market. Maybe in the primary market when the next big deal comes. We haven't seen any large blocks of Florida GO's here."
In debt futures, the June municipal contract ended up 5/32 at 112-9/32. The June T-bond contract ended up 2/32 at 107-20/32.
The U.S. Treasury's benchmark 30-year bond closed up 2/32 at 94-16/32 to yield 7.07 percent.

Thursday's new issue action was light. On the negotiated side, Wheat First Butcher Singer repriced $29 million Norfolk Industrial Development Authority, Va., bonds, raising yields in several maturities.
